title: Git Workflows & Trunk-Based Development
summary: Best practices for atomic commits, short-lived branches, clean rebases, and high-velocity team collaboration.
keyPrinciples: Short-lived branches: merge into trunk frequently (multiple times daily) to eliminate painful merge conflicts.
Conventional Commits: write structured commit messages that enable automated changelog generation.
Atomic commits: each commit represents a single logical change that leaves the test suite green.

rules.title: Write Descriptive Conventional Commit Messages
rules.description: Avoid vague commit messages like 'fixed stuff' or 'WIP'. Use standard type prefixes (`feat:`, `fix:`, `refactor:`, `docs:`, `test:`) with clear imperative explanations.

badExample.code:
// Bad: Meaningless commit history
git commit -m "fixes"
git commit -m "update api"
git commit -m "wip more changes"
badExample.explanation: Impossible to tell what changed, why it changed, or whether it includes a breaking contract alteration.

goodExample.explanation: Instantly communicates scope, category, and precise business intent.

productionChecklist: Trunk branch (`main`) is always deployable to production.
Feature branches live for less than 48 hours before merging.
Pull requests include clear screenshots or test proofs.
Rebase on top of `origin/main` before opening PR to ensure linear history.
